stories.text: The US has approved selling 500 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine, the only effective defence against Russian ballistic missiles.
Prime Minister Burnham says he is open to a UK apology for the transatlantic slave trade, but rejects paying reparations.
Suspected North Korean hackers are the main suspects in a record-breaking theft from the crypto exchange Binance.
Home Secretary Mahmood is expected to change indefinite leave to remain rules for migrant workers, despite opposition inside the government.
The second series of Celebrity Traitors ended on Friday with a tense final, after drawing 15 million viewers.
Police were sent in amid a standoff over Poland's top court, after the government suspended two senior judges and sought criminal charges.
Karl Bushby, who set off to walk around the world 28 years ago, is nearly home after covering 36,000 miles.
The G20 group photo was scrapped after protests over Russia's minister, whom UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband accused of killing Ukrainian civilians.
Talk of an early general election continues among MPs at Westminster, even though Prime Minister Burnham has firmly ruled one out.
International talks on halting the decline of nature have reached an agreement, but questions over funding remain unresolved.
